title: The Rum Boogie, Lefty Bates and the start of Jazz Limited
summary: Rum Boogie with Dyett, Lefty Bates from 1951 to 1959, then Jazz Limited.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, after Earl Fuller, --
Walter Fuller.
Walter Fuller, right. Where -- what happened then? Now, the War is going on by this time.
The war's going on then. That's during the time -- see, now, that was in '41, '42, '43, '44. Then I went to the Rum Boogie.
Yeah, where was that?
(Duke)
55th Street and Calumet. I worked with Myer Young (PHONETIC), and Captain Dyett -- Walter Dyett
He had the band there?
He had the band then. That was during the war.
And again, it was shows and --
Yeah.
Did they have breakfast dances out there?
Yeah, we had breakfast dances. That's right. I think our breakfast dancing was Sunday morning, out there.
What was that other club out 55th Street, Red Saunders was at so long?
You mean the DeLisa.
Yeah, the DeLisa. Wasn't that near there?
Yeah. Well, that was -- let's see, that was at 55th and State. We were at 55th and Calumet. That was about five or six blocks.
Well, when did you go with Lefty Bates?
I went with Lefty Bates in '51.
And again, that was sort of enter-
Entertainment, yeah.
And when did you go with Jazz, Limited?
'59. That was --
Yeah, I left Lefty Bates in '59, and that's when I started Jazz, Limited.
And then you were playing mostly tuba?
Yeah.
